ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a city–suburb cross-sectional climate data diagram from the NW to SE direction, with positions such as ①②, urban area, ③④ marked horizontally. The left vertical axis is temperature, and the right vertical axis is annual precipitation. The July average temperature curve is relatively high near the urban area and ③, and declines at ④; the January average temperature curve is also relatively higher near ③; the annual precipitation curve remains relatively high near the urban area and ③, while it is relatively low near ② and ④. Then reason: heavy chemical industrial areas usually emit waste heat and a large amount of dust, causing industrial climate anomalies with relatively high temperature and relatively much precipitation at and near the location. Comparing ①②③④, ③ is located in the near suburbs on the southeast side of the urban area, and in the figure both temperature and annual precipitation near ③ are still relatively high, which better fits the climate characteristics caused by a heavy chemical industrial area than the far suburb ④ and the northwest-side suburbs. Therefore, the heavy chemical industrial area of this city is most likely located at ③.
